sources.note: C4 accelerates diffusion language model decoding with two separate gates: one that decides when the whole sequence may stop, by checking that the extracted answer span is both confident and unchanged for several steps, and one that decides which token positions a step may commit, by committing only a boundary-anchored run and confirming deferred positions one step later.
sources.title: Commit Locally, Exit Globally: Coordinating Adaptive Sampling and Early Exit in Diffusion Language Models

sources.note: ParoQuant is a 4-bit weight-only post-training quantization method that applies a series of independent Givens (pairwise) rotations plus channel-wise scaling to weights before quantization, with a fused CUDA kernel, in order to keep accuracy on reasoning benchmarks where quantization error accumulates over long chains of thought.
sources.title: ParoQuant: Pairwise Rotation Quantization for Efficient Reasoning LLM Inference

result.definition: The two sources use 'C4' for two entirely unrelated things that share a name, and nothing here connects them. In 'Commit Locally, Exit Globally', C4 is a decoding method for diffusion language models built from two gates with matched scopes: CVEE decides when the whole sequence may stop, firing when the extracted answer span is confident and has been unchanged for several steps, and CCTC decides which positions a step may commit, committing only a boundary-anchored run and confirming deferred positions one step later. It reports end-to-end speedups of 2.6x-18.6x on LLaDA-8B-Instruct and Dream-7B-Instruct across 12 tasks, with paired McNemar tests finding no statistically significant accuracy difference from full decoding in any cell. In ParoQuant, by contrast, C4 is simply the web-crawl corpus used as a perplexity evaluation set alongside WikiText2, and has nothing to do with early exit.
